prompt: Return a single column `sec` = the second-highest DISTINCT salary from employees, or NULL if none.
schema: CREATE TABLE employees(id INTEGER, salary INTEGER);INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,100),(2,200),(3,200),(4,300);
reference: SELECT MAX(salary) AS sec FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees)

prompt: From txns(acct,day,amt) return acct, day, and a running total `rt` of amt per acct ordered by day. Order rows by acct, day.
schema: CREATE TABLE txns(acct TEXT, day INTEGER, amt INTEGER);INSERT INTO txns VALUES ('a',1,10),('a',2,20),('a',3,5),('b',1,7),('b',2,3);
reference: SELECT acct, day, SUM(amt) OVER (PARTITION BY acct ORDER BY day) AS rt FROM txns ORDER BY acct, day

prompt: From scores(player,game,pts) return the single highest-pts row per game (ties: lowest player alphabetically). Columns game, player, pts ordered by game.
schema: CREATE TABLE scores(player TEXT, game TEXT, pts INTEGER);INSERT INTO scores VALUES ('ann','x',5),('bob','x',9),('cid','x',9),('ann','y',3),('bob','y',1);
reference: SELECT game, player, pts FROM (SELECT player,game,pts, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY pts DESC, player ASC) rn FROM scores) t WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY game

prompt: logins(uid,d) has integer day numbers. For uid='u' return the length `len` of each maximal run of consecutive days, ordered by the run's first day.
schema: CREATE TABLE logins(uid TEXT, d INTEGER);INSERT INTO logins VALUES ('u',1),('u',2),('u',3),('u',5),('u',6),('u',9);
reference: SELECT COUNT(*) AS len FROM (SELECT d, d - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY d) AS grp FROM logins WHERE uid='u') t GROUP BY grp ORDER BY MIN(d)

prompt: From series(t,v) return t and the 3-point trailing moving average `ma` (current and up to 2 prior rows by t). Order by t. ma is a real number.
schema: CREATE TABLE series(t INTEGER, v INTEGER);INSERT INTO series VALUES (1,3),(2,6),(3,9),(4,12);
reference: SELECT t, AVG(v*1.0) OVER (ORDER BY t ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ma FROM series ORDER BY t

prompt: events(uid,ts,status) may have many rows per uid. Return the latest (max ts) status per uid as columns uid,status ordered by uid.
schema: CREATE TABLE events(uid TEXT, ts INTEGER, status TEXT);INSERT INTO events VALUES ('a',1,'new'),('a',3,'done'),('a',2,'wip'),('b',1,'new');
reference: SELECT uid, status FROM (SELECT uid,status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY uid ORDER BY ts DESC) rn FROM events) t WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY uid

prompt: Return names of customers(id,name) that have NO row in orders(cid). Column name, ordered by name.
schema: CREATE TABLE customers(id INTEGER, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders(oid INTEGER, cid INTEGER);INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'ann'),(2,'bob'),(3,'cid');INSERT INTO orders VALUES (10,1),(11,1),(12,3);
reference: SELECT name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.cid=c.id) ORDER BY name

prompt: rev(mon,amt) has monthly revenue (mon is 1..N). Return mon and month-over-month delta `d` (amt minus previous month's amt; NULL for first). Order by mon.
schema: CREATE TABLE rev(mon INTEGER, amt INTEGER);INSERT INTO rev VALUES (1,100),(2,150),(3,120);
reference: SELECT mon, amt - LAG(amt) OVER (ORDER BY mon) AS d FROM rev ORDER BY mon

prompt: employees(id,dept,salary). For each dept that has at least 2 distinct salaries, return dept and sec = the second-highest DISTINCT salary in that dept. Order by dept.
schema: CREATE TABLE employees(id INTEGER, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER);INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'eng',100),(2,'eng',200),(3,'eng',200),(4,'eng',300),(5,'sales',50),(6,'sales',50),(7,'sales',80);
reference: SELECT e1.dept AS dept, MAX(e1.salary) AS sec FROM employees e1 WHERE e1.salary < (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.dept = e1.dept) GROUP BY e1.dept ORDER BY e1.dept

prompt: scores(player,subject,score). For subject='math' return player and rnk = the standings rank by score DESC (ties share the same rank, next rank skips accordingly). Order rows by rnk then player.
schema: CREATE TABLE scores(player TEXT, subject TEXT, score INTEGER);INSERT INTO scores VALUES ('alice','math',90),('bob','math',90),('cid','math',80),('dan','math',70),('eve','sci',50);
reference: SELECT player, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rnk FROM scores WHERE subject='math' ORDER BY rnk, player

prompt: orders(oid,cid). Return cid and cnt = number of orders, for customers whose order count is strictly greater than the average order count across all customers who have at least one order. Order by cid.
schema: CREATE TABLE orders(oid INTEGER, cid INTEGER);INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1),(2,1),(3,1),(4,2),(5,3),(6,3);
reference: SELECT cid, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders GROUP BY cid HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders GROUP BY cid) t) ORDER BY cid

prompt: emp(id,name,manager_id). Return emp = employee name and mgr = their manager's name, for employees that have a manager. Order by emp.
schema: CREATE TABLE emp(id INTEGER, name TEXT, manager_id INTEGER);INSERT INTO emp VALUES (1,'alice',NULL),(2,'bob',1),(3,'cid',1),(4,'dan',2);
reference: SELECT e.name AS emp, m.name AS mgr FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.manager_id = m.id ORDER BY e.name

prompt: sales(id,region,amt). Return id, region, amt, and pct = amt as a fraction of the SUM of all amt (a real number, not multiplied by 100). Order by id.
schema: CREATE TABLE sales(id INTEGER, region TEXT, amt INTEGER);INSERT INTO sales VALUES (1,'r1',100),(2,'r1',300),(3,'r2',600);
reference: SELECT id, region, amt, amt*1.0/SUM(amt) OVER () AS pct FROM sales ORDER BY id

prompt: users(id,email). Return email and cnt = count of rows, for emails that appear more than once. Order by email.
schema: CREATE TABLE users(id INTEGER, email TEXT);INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'a@x.com'),(2,'b@x.com'),(3,'a@x.com'),(4,'c@x.com'),(5,'a@x.com'),(6,'d@x.com'),(7,'d@x.com');
reference: SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY email

prompt: events(id,uid,ts,val). For each uid return uid, first_val = val of the row with the earliest ts, and last_val = val of the row with the latest ts. One row per uid, ordered by uid.
schema: CREATE TABLE events(id INTEGER, uid TEXT, ts INTEGER, val INTEGER);INSERT INTO events VALUES (1,'a',1,10),(2,'a',2,20),(3,'a',3,5),(4,'b',1,7);
reference: SELECT uid, (SELECT val FROM events e2 WHERE e2.uid=e1.uid ORDER BY ts ASC LIMIT 1) AS first_val, (SELECT val FROM events e2 WHERE e2.uid=e1.uid ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_val FROM events e1 GROUP BY uid ORDER BY uid

prompt: products(pid,name), inventory(pid,qty,reorder_level). Return name of products whose inventory qty is strictly below reorder_level. Order by name.
schema: CREATE TABLE products(pid INTEGER, name TEXT);CREATE TABLE inventory(pid INTEGER, qty INTEGER, reorder_level INTEGER);INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'widget'),(2,'gadget'),(3,'gizmo');INSERT INTO inventory VALUES (1,5,10),(2,20,10),(3,3,3);
reference: SELECT p.name AS name FROM products p JOIN inventory i ON p.pid=i.pid WHERE i.qty < i.reorder_level ORDER BY p.name

prompt: orders2(oid,cid,status). Return cid, done_cnt = count of that customer's orders with status='done', and pending_cnt = count with status='pending' (0 if none, not NULL). Order by cid.
schema: CREATE TABLE orders2(oid INTEGER, cid INTEGER, status TEXT);INSERT INTO orders2 VALUES (1,1,'done'),(2,1,'done'),(3,1,'pending'),(4,2,'pending'),(5,2,'cancelled');
reference: SELECT cid, SUM(CASE WHEN status='done' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS done_cnt, SUM(CASE WHEN status='pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pending_cnt FROM orders2 GROUP BY cid ORDER BY cid

prompt: customers(cid,name), orders3(oid,cid), order_items(oid,category,amt). Return customer name and total = SUM(amt) across all their order_items (via customers -> orders3 -> order_items). Only include customers with at least one order_item. Order by name.
schema: CREATE TABLE customers(cid INTEGER, name TEXT);CREATE TABLE orders3(oid INTEGER, cid INTEGER);CREATE TABLE order_items(oid INTEGER, category TEXT, amt INTEGER);INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'ann'),(2,'bob'),(3,'cid');INSERT INTO orders3 VALUES (1,1),(2,2);INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,'elec',100),(1,'book',20),(2,'elec',50);
reference: SELECT c.name AS name, SUM(oi.amt) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders3 o ON o.cid=c.cid JOIN order_items oi ON oi.oid=o.oid GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name

prompt: employees2(id,dept,salary). Return id, dept, salary, and diff = salary minus the average salary within that dept (a real number, via a window function). Order by id.
schema: CREATE TABLE employees2(id INTEGER, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER);INSERT INTO employees2 VALUES (1,'eng',100),(2,'eng',200),(3,'eng',300),(4,'sales',50),(5,'sales',150);
reference: SELECT id, dept, salary, salary - AVG(salary*1.0) OVER (PARTITION BY dept) AS diff FROM employees2 ORDER BY id
